question: Which statement best describes Variables?
options: Sass variables ($name: value) store reusable values like colors, spacing, and fonts so you change a design decision in one place. They are resolved at COMPILE time (baked into the output), unlike CSS custom properties which live at runtime in the cascade. Sass variables are great for build-time configuration; custom properties are better when values must change dynamically (themes, JS).

Sass ships built-in functions (math, color manipulation like lighten()/darken()/mix(), string and list helpers) and lets you define your own with @function to return computed values. Functions return a value to use in a property, whereas mixins emit whole declaration blocks. They power things like generating a tint scale from one base color.

Mixins (@mixin / @include) are reusable blocks of declarations, optionally parameterized, that you inject into rules — like functions that output CSS. They DRY up repeated patterns (flex centering, media-query helpers, button bases). Unlike @extend, a mixin duplicates its output per call, which keeps selectors independent at the cost of some repetition in the compiled CSS.

Sass lets you nest selectors to mirror HTML structure, and the & placeholder references the parent selector (great for BEM modifiers and states). It reduces repetition and groups related rules. Caution: deep nesting inflates specificity and produces long descendant selectors, so keep it shallow — usually one or two levels.

Partials are files prefixed with an underscore (_buttons.scss) that aren't compiled on their own but are imported into a main stylesheet, letting you split CSS into modular files. question: Which statement best describes Mixins?
options: Sass has real programming constructs: @if/@else, @each, @for, and @while, plus maps and lists. options: Preprocessors are not understood by browsers; a compiler (Dart Sass, or a bundler plugin) transforms .scss into plain .css before deployment. This adds tooling: a build/watch process, source maps for debugging, and a dependency on the toolchain. Native CSS has absorbed several preprocessor features: custom properties (--var) for runtime variables, native CSS nesting, @layer for cascade control, color-mix() and relative colors, calc() and clamp() for math, and @container queries.
